summary: This document defines Mobile IP Agent Advertisement and Registration Request extensions that let a foreign agent challenge a mobile node, giving replay protection and allowing methods such as CHAP. It also adds a Mobile-AAA Authentication extension so a node can supply credentials through AAA infrastructure. It replaces RFC 3012 and updates RFC 3344.

plainLanguage.summary: When a laptop joins a network away from home, it must prove who it is. This RFC adds a challenge to that exchange: the foreign agent sends a random number, and the laptop has to use that exact number in its reply. An old recorded reply no longer works, because it carries an old number.

how does mobile ip prevent replay attacks
what is the mobile aaa authentication extension
what is challenge window in mobile ip
subtitle: How a visiting mobile device proves it is not replaying an old registration, and how it can reach a central account server.

tldr.problem: The Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension in Mobile IPv4 gives a foreign agent no direct guarantee that a registration is not a replay, and it cannot use existing methods such as CHAP to authenticate portable computers.
tldr.mechanism: The foreign agent puts a random Challenge value in its Agent Advertisements and Registration Replies. The mobile node copies that value into a Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension and adds an authentication extension, optionally a new Mobile-AAA extension that lets an AAA server check the node's credentials.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4721 is a Proposed Standard from January 2007. It obsoletes RFC 3012, adds the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension to RFC 3344, and defines seven error codes for the cases where a challenge is missing, unknown, stale or answered with a bad authenticator.

today: RFC 4721 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2007. It obsoletes RFC 3012 and updates RFC 3344, and no later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Mobile IP defines the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension, which lets a mobile node authenticate itself to a foreign agent. The RFC is direct about its limits: that extension gives the foreign agent no direct guarantee that the protocol is protected from replays, and it does not allow existing techniques such as the Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol (CHAP) to be used for authenticating portable computer devices.

This document defines extensions to the Mobile IP Agent Advertisement and the Registration Request that let a foreign agent use a challenge/response mechanism to authenticate the mobile node. It also updates RFC 3344 by adding a Mobile-Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) Authentication extension, so a mobile node can supply credentials for authorization using commonly available AAA infrastructure. That extension MAY co-exist in the same Registration Request with the authentication extensions defined for Mobile IP in RFC 3344. The document obsoletes RFC 3012.

The RFC also defines a small vocabulary for the challenges. A previously used challenge is one the mobile node sent in an earlier Registration Request that passed all the foreign agent's validity checks. An unknown challenge is one the foreign agent has no record of having advertised to that mobile node. An unused challenge is neither unknown nor previously used.
sections.plainLanguage: Mobile IP lets a laptop authenticate itself to the foreign agent it visits, but the built-in method cannot promise the agent that the registration is fresh. This RFC adds a challenge the agent issues itself, and a new extension that lets the agent check the laptop's credentials against a central account server.

sections.title: The Challenge Extension in Agent Advertisements
sections.content:
The RFC defines a new extension to the Router Discovery Protocol, RFC 1256, for foreign agents that need to issue a challenge. The extension has three fields: a Type field with the value 24, a Length field giving the length of the Challenge value in octets, which SHOULD be at least 4, and the Challenge field itself, a random value that SHOULD be at least 32 bits.

The foreign agent inserts this extension into its Agent Advertisements to communicate a previously unused challenge value that the mobile node can use to compute an authentication for its next registration request. The challenge is chosen by the foreign agent to give local assurance that the mobile node is not replaying an earlier registration request. RFC 4086 gives more information on generating pseudo-random numbers suitable for such values. How a mobile node stores challenges received from several foreign agents is implementation specific and out of scope.

A solicited Agent Advertisement needs extra care. If the solicited advertisement is multicast, the foreign agent MUST NOT generate a new Challenge value or update its window of remembered advertised challenges; it must re-use the most recent of the CHALLENGE_WINDOW values. If the advertisement is unicast back to the soliciting mobile node, and the challenge most recently unicast to that node has not been previously used, it SHOULD be repeated. Otherwise a new challenge MUST be generated and remembered as the most recent challenge issued to that mobile node.
sections.plainLanguage: The foreign agent puts a random number into its Agent Advertisements. The number should be at least 32 bits long, and the length field should say at least 4 octets. A multicast advertisement reuses the recent challenge rather than making a new one, so that many nodes share one value.

sections.title: The Registration Exchange
sections.content:
When the mobile node receives an Agent Advertisement that contains the Challenge extension and it has no security association with the foreign agent, it MUST include the challenge value in a Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension in its Registration Request. If it does have a security association, it SHOULD still include the value. When the Registration Request contains the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension, the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension MUST follow it. If both Mobile-Foreign Authentication and Mobile-AAA Authentication extensions are present, the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension MUST come first, then the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension, then the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension. In every case the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension and the authentication extension that follows it MUST follow the Mobile-Home Authentication extension, if present.

On receiving the Registration Request, a foreign agent that has issued a challenge and has no security association with the node SHOULD check that the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension exists and holds a value the node has not used before. If the extension is missing, the agent MUST reply with the code missing_challenge. The agent MUST NOT accept a challenge that was not offered in the last Registration Reply or unicast Agent Advertisement, or advertised as one of the last CHALLENGE_WINDOW values in the immediately preceding Agent Advertisements; otherwise it SHOULD reply with unknown_challenge. If the node replays a value it used before, the agent SHOULD reply with stale_challenge.

The agent MUST also check that a Mobile-Foreign or Mobile-AAA Authentication extension follows the challenge extension. A registration message that carries the challenge without one of those authentication extensions MUST be silently discarded. If the authenticator in a Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension fails verification, the agent MAY reply with mobile node failed authentication. If the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension fails verification, it MAY reply with fa_bad_aaa_auth. When the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension is present, the foreign agent MUST NOT remove the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension and the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension before forwarding the request to the home agent.

The foreign agent SHOULD include a new Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension in any Registration Reply, successful or not, so that the node can re-register without waiting for another advertisement. The home agent, on receiving a request with the Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension, MUST include the challenge extension in its Registration Reply, placed after the Mobile-Home authentication extension, and the extension SHOULD be authenticated by a Foreign-Home Authentication extension. Because the extension type 132 falls in the range 128-255, the home agent MUST process such a request even if it does not recognize the extension.
sections.plainLanguage: The mobile node copies the advertised challenge into its Registration Request and adds an authentication extension. The foreign agent checks that the challenge is one it recently offered and has not already accepted, then relays the request to the home agent and passes a challenge back in the reply so the node has a fresh value for next time.

sections.title: Challenge and Authentication Extensions
sections.content:
The Mobile-Foreign Challenge extension is a new Mobile IP Registration extension used to satisfy a challenge that appeared in an Agent Advertisement. Its Type is 132, which is skippable, so a node that does not understand it can ignore it. Its Length field gives the length of the Challenge value, and the Challenge field is copied from the received Challenge extension.

Once the mobile node has registered successfully with one of the CHALLENGE_WINDOW values advertised by the foreign agent, in any new Registration Request it MUST NOT use any challenge value that the foreign agent advertised before the value in its last Registration Request. This is the rule that makes a stored old registration useless to an attacker.

The Generalized Mobile IP Authentication extension collects the data for new authentication applications into one extension type with subtypes, because the base Mobile IP specification only defines authentication against the home agent and the foreign agent. It has a Type of 36, which is not skippable, a Subtype field that identifies the kind of endpoints or other characteristics of the authentication strategy, a Length field that is 4 plus the number of octets in the Authenticator and MUST be at least 20, a 32-bit Security Parameters Index (SPI), and a variable-length Authenticator field. Only one subtype is defined here: 1, the Mobile-AAA Authentication subtype, which uses HMAC-MD5.
sections.plainLanguage: The challenge extension carries the random value from the advertisement into the registration. The generalized authentication extension is a single container that holds the credentials, with a subtype that says what kind of authentication is inside it. Only one subtype is defined here, the Mobile-AAA one.

sections.title: The Mobile-AAA Extension and the Authenticator
sections.content:
The mobile node MAY include a Mobile-AAA Authentication extension in any Registration Request. If the node does not include a Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension, it MUST include the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension whenever the challenge extension is present. If both are present, the Mobile-AAA extension MUST precede the Mobile-Foreign Authentication extension, and the Mobile-Home Authentication extension MUST appear before the Mobile-AAA extension. The corresponding response MUST include the Mobile-Home Authentication extension and MUST NOT include the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension.

The default algorithm for computing the authenticator is HMAC-MD5, RFC 2104, computed over the preceding Mobile IP data, that is the UDP payload and all prior extensions in their entirety, followed by the Type, Subtype, Length and SPI fields, in that order. Each mobile node MUST support producing the authenticator this way, and it must be possible to configure any arbitrary 32-bit SPI outside the reserved range 0-255 to select another algorithm.

A second method exists for AAA servers that admit only a single security association and so ignore the SPI numbers, a common situation with RADIUS servers. The SPI number CHAP_SPI is reserved for it. The authenticator is computed by applying MD5, RFC 1321, to the high-order octet of the challenge, then the key, then the MD5 of the preceding Mobile IP data with the Type, Subtype, Length and SPI fields, then the least-order 237 octets of the challenge. Since the RADIUS protocol cannot carry attributes longer than 253 octets, the preceding data is hashed with MD5. If the challenge has fewer than 238 octets, the high-order octet is used twice, and no padding is added to lengthen the challenge. In co-located care-of address mode the challenge value 0 is used.
sections.plainLanguage: The authenticator is a keyed hash. By default it is HMAC-MD5 over the registration message so far plus the extension's own header fields. A second, older method uses plain MD5 in a way that matches what RADIUS servers expect, so a site that only supports RADIUS can still check the node's credentials.

sections.title: Configurable Parameters and Error Values
sections.content:
Every Mobile IP agent supporting these extensions SHOULD be able to configure each of two parameters. CHALLENGE_WINDOW has a default value of 2 and first appears in Section 3.2; it SHOULD be at least 2, which makes it far less likely that mobile nodes register with a challenge value outside the set the foreign agent allows. CHAP_SPI has a default value of 2 and first appears in Section 8.

The RFC defines a set of error codes for the Registration Reply. unknown_challenge is 104, mobile node failed authentication is 67, missing_challenge is 105, stale_challenge is 106, fa_bad_aaa_auth is 108, ha_bad_aaa_auth is 144 and ha_wrong_challenge is 109. The values correspond to the range conventionally associated with rejection by the foreign agent, 64-127, and the code 67 is a pre-existing value from RFC 3344. The ha_wrong_challenge code may also appear in the Status code of the Foreign Agent Error extension defined in RFC 4636.

For IANA, the Generalized Mobile IP Authentication extension is assigned the value 36, and a new number space is created for enumerating its subtypes. Subtypes other than 1, the Mobile-AAA Authentication extension, must be specified and approved by a designated expert. The Mobile Node to Foreign Agent Challenge extension is a router advertisement extension and has been assigned the value 132. The CHAP_SPI number 2 comes from the reserved range of SPI numbers 0-255, where new assignments must be approved by the Mobile IP working group; SPI number 1 should not be assigned unless the working group decides that SKIP is not important, and SPI number 0 should not be assigned.
sections.plainLanguage: Two settings tune the behaviour: how many recent challenges the agent keeps, and which SPI selects the CHAP-style computation. Seven error codes report a missing, unknown, stale or badly answered challenge, and the new extension numbers are registered with IANA.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
If a malicious mobile node replays the authenticator for an old Mobile-Foreign Challenge, the foreign agent detects it, because the agent always checks whether it has recently advertised that challenge. Allowing mobile nodes with different IP addresses or NAIs to use the same challenge value is not a vulnerability, because the authentication data is computed over data that differs between them, the mobile node's IP address at least.

If the foreign agent chooses a challenge value with fewer than 4 octets, it SHOULD also record the value of the Identification field for the mobile node, so that it can tell whether later messages using that short challenge are genuinely new.

The CHAP-style method in Section 8 uses MD5 in a way that is less secure than HMAC-MD5 and MUST be avoided whenever possible.

An active attacker may try to prevent successful registrations by sending many Agent Solicitations or bogus Registration Requests, each of which could cause the foreign agent to answer with a fresh challenge and so invalidate the challenge the mobile node is trying to use. To prevent this, the foreign agent MUST NOT invalidate previously unused challenges when responding to unauthenticated Registration Requests or Agent Solicitations, and it MUST NOT allocate new storage when answering such messages, since that would also allow a denial of service.

The Challenge extension need not be used in co-located care-of address mode, because replay protection there is provided by the Identification field in the Registration Request. The subtype field of the Generalized Mobile IP Authentication extension identifies the characteristics of the authentication strategy, and only one subtype is defined here, the Mobile-AAA subtype that uses HMAC-MD5. Moving to a new message authentication algorithm later would be done by defining a new subtype.
sections.plainLanguage: Replaying an old challenge fails because the agent only accepts challenges it recently issued. The RFC also warns that flooding the agent with bogus registrations could invalidate the challenge a real node is using, so the agent must keep its unused challenges and must not store new state for unauthenticated messages.
